title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option P4: Superpower relations and the Cold War, 1941–91

exam_structure.overview: Tests unfolding period narrative across 3 Key Topics. Q1 Explain two consequences (8m), Q2 Write an analytical narrative (8m), Q3 Explain the importance of two events (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: The origins of the Cold War, 1941–58

topics.title: 1. Early tension between East and West
points: The Grand Alliance; outcomes of the Tehran, Yalta & Potsdam conferences
Ideological differences between the superpowers & the attitudes of Stalin, Truman & Churchill
Impact on US-Soviet relations of the development of the atomic bomb, the Long & Novikov telegrams & the creation of Soviet satellite states in Eastern Europe

topics.title: 2. The development of the Cold War
points: Impact on US-Soviet relations of the Truman Doctrine & the Marshall Plan, 1947
Significance: Cominform (1947), Comecon (1949) & the formation of NATO (1949)
Berlin: its division into zones; The Berlin Crisis (blockade & airlift) of 1948-49 & its impact; formation of the Federal Republic of Germany & German Democratic Republic

topics.title: 3. The Cold War intensifies
points: Significance: arms race; formation of the Warsaw Pact
Events in 1956 leading to the Hungarian Uprising & Khrushchev’s response
International reaction to the Soviet invasion of Hungary

topics.title: 1. Increased tension between East and West
points: Refugee problem in Berlin, Khrushchev’s Berlin ultimatum (1958) & the summit meetings of 1959–61

Impact of the Cuban Revolution on relations with the USA & the Soviet Union (incl. the refusal of the USA to recognise Castro’s government & the closer relations with the Soviet Union); Bay of Pigs incident
Opposition in Czechoslovakia to Soviet control: the Prague Spring

topics.title: 2. Cold War crises
points: Construction of the Berlin Wall, 1961
Events of the Cuban Missile Crisis
The Brezhnev Doctrine & the re-establishment of Soviet control in Czechoslovakia

topics.title: 3. Reaction to crisis
points: Impact of the construction of the Berlin Wall on US-Soviet relations; Kennedy’s visit to West Berlin in 1963

Consequences of the Cuban Missile Crisis (incl. the ‘hotline’); Attempts at arms control: the Limited Test Ban Treaty (1963); the Outer Space Treaty (1967); & the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (1968)
International reaction to Soviet measures in Czechoslovakia

sections.title: Key topic 3: The end of the Cold War, 1970–91

topics.title: 1. Attempts to reduce superpower tensions in the 1970s
points: Détente & attempts to reduce tensions in the 1970s
Significance: SALT 1, the Helsinki Accords & SALT 2

topics.title: 2. The end of détente and the ‘Second Cold War’
points: Significance: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, the Carter Doctrine & the Olympic boycotts
Reagan & the ‘Second Cold War’, the Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI)
Significance: Reagan & Gorbachev in reducing tensions

topics.title: 3. The collapse of Soviet control of Eastern Europe, 1985-91
points: Impact of Gorbachev’s ‘new thinking’ on Eastern Europe: the loosening Soviet grip on Eastern Europe
Significance: fall of the Berlin Wall
Collapse of the Soviet Union & its significance in bringing about the end of the Warsaw Pact
